name: Sherpani Col
gearList: Figure-8 or ATC guide belay/rappel device
High altitude mountaineering double boots (6000m+ rated)
objectiveHazards: Deep crevasse fields on the Upper Barun Glacier
Steep 45° to 50° hard-packed ice wall ascent
High bergschrund crossing requiring bridging/anchors
Rapidly fluctuating whiteout storms and high-altitude hypoxia
tacticalAdvice: Cross the lower glacier before 09:00 AM when the snow bridges are hard-frozen. Fix ropes on the steep bergschrund headwall the evening before or early in the alpine dawn. Ensure porter safety with harnesses clipped into fixed lines.
historicalNote: First crossed in 1954 by Michael Ward and Sir Edmund Hillary during the British Everest/Barun exploration expedition.

name: West Col
grade: Alpine Grade D / III (Highest Point on GHT)
objectiveHazards: 6,190m extreme altitude causing rapid exhaustion
Sheer 150m vertical ice and rock headwall descent down into the Hongu Basin
Hanging séracs and rock discharge along the couloir
No shelter on the col; exposed to hurricane-force jet stream winds
tacticalAdvice: The descent from West Col onto the Hongu Glacier is the single most demanding technical pitch on the GHT High Route. Establish solid deadman or snow-picket snow anchors on the crest and inspect rope chafing over rock edges before rappelling.
historicalNote: Forms the second col of the legendary 'Three Cols'. Traverses between the Barun and the pristine, uninhabited Hongu Valley.

name: Amphu Labsta
technicalLevel: Very Severe (Steep Ice Fall & Cornice Rappel)
fixedRopesRequired: Yes (60m - 100m fixed line on north ice face)
objectiveHazards: Giant unstable ice cornices guarding the pass summit
Steep 80m vertical ice chimney abseil on the Khumbu side
Frequent rockfall triggered by afternoon sun warming the cliffs above
tacticalAdvice: Ascend from the Hongu side early before dawn. Lower heavy expedition packs down the steep ice chute on the north side via rope pulley before climbers descend to minimize anchor load.
historicalNote: The final link of the 'Three Cols', dropping directly from the wild Hongu basin into Chhukung in the shadow of Ama Dablam.

name: Tashi Laptsa Pass
gearList: Helmet (mandatory due to loose rock shooting gallery)
High altitude 4-season tent and sub-zero sleeping bag
objectiveHazards: Extensive heavily crevassed Drolambau Glacier
Unstable loose scree and falling boulders on the Thame descent
Frequent blizzard whitewashes crossing the high glacier plateau
tacticalAdvice: The descent into Khumbu passes through an active rockfall gully. Wear helmets at all times and cross quickly in single file without pausing.
historicalNote: A historic sacred link between the Sherpas of Rolwaling and Khumbu, guarded by the peak Pachermo (6,273m).

name: Tilman Pass
fixedRopesRequired: Optional / helpful on steep snow slope
objectiveHazards: Completely unmarked route over loose lateral moraines
Snow-covered hidden crevasses on the upper glacier
Zero cellular coverage and total isolation between Kyanjin and Panch Pokhari
tacticalAdvice: Named after legendary British mountaineer Bill Tilman who explored it in 1949. Camp at Tin Pokhari on the south side. Carry a satellite messenger (Garmin inReach).
historicalNote: Bill Tilman discovered this pass while seeking an alternative exit route from the Langtang valley to Kathmandu.

name: Teri La
fixedRopesRequired: Not required, but terrain is extremely loose scree
gearList: 6 to 8 days of dehydrated mountain rations
objectiveHazards: Absolute absence of human habitation or tea huts for 6 consecutive days
High desert dehydration and blistering UV index above 5,000m
Loose, collapsing shale scree ramps on the pass approaches
tacticalAdvice: Acclimatize thoroughly in Naar and Phu before committing to the pass. Ensure your support team carries enough kerosene/white gas because there is zero firewood in the rainshadow desert.
historicalNote: Opened as a trekking route only recently; provides the ultimate high-altitude bridge between Manang's Tibetan enclave and the walled Kingdom of Lo.

name: Larkya La
gearList: Microspikes / crampons for early morning frozen snow
objectiveHazards: Very long, gradual moraine ascent starting at 04:00 AM
Intense freezing headwinds on the broad summit plateau
Icy switchbacks on the steep 1,400m descent to Bimthang
tacticalAdvice: Dharamsala (high camp) is crowded and primitive. Start early before 04:30 AM to reach the pass by sunrise for unobstructed views of Himlung Himal, Cheo Himal, and Annapurna II.
historicalNote: Historic salt and wool trade route between Tibet and the Gorkha region of Nepal.

name: Thorong La
objectiveHazards: Severe acute mountain sickness (AMS) risk if acclimatization was rushed
Sudden blizzard whiteouts (Hudhud storm disaster site in 2014)
1,600m continuous knee-jarring descent to Muktinath
tacticalAdvice: Check weather forecasts closely. Never attempt crossing during active snowfall or impending cyclone depressions. Hydrate with at least 4 liters of fluid per day.
historicalNote: The most famous and traversed 5,000m pass in Nepal, linking the lush Marshyangdi Valley with the arid Kali Gandaki gorge.

name: Sangda La / Jungben La
objectiveHazards: Extreme isolation; evacuation takes days if weather grounds helicopters
Freezing night temperatures dropping to -25°C in late autumn
Vast expanses of featureless high plateau scree
tacticalAdvice: This pass bridges Mustang into the mystical plateau of Chharka Bhot in Dolpo. Hire experienced local Dolpo-pa horsemen who know the seasonal water points.
historicalNote: Featured in Peter Matthiessen's acclaimed book 'The Snow Leopard' and Eric Valli's Oscar-nominated film 'Himalaya'.

name: Kagmara La
objectiveHazards: Boulder hopping along glacial outflow rivers
Lingering snowfields into early summer on the northern aspect
Remote location with sparse local settlements
tacticalAdvice: Offers staggering panoramas of the Kanjiroba range. Descend to the scenic Kaigaon village and experience traditional Khas cultural hospitality.
historicalNote: Gateway between the Shey Phoksundo National Park and the high coniferous ridges leading into Rara.
